quinnipiacSettled.name: Quinnipiac settlement
quinnipiacSettled.description: A group of London merchants and their families heard of the area around the Quinnipiac River and settled the area, calling it Quinnipiac or Quinipiek.

quinnipiacRenamedNewHaven.name: Quinnipiac settlement renamed to New Haven
quinnipiacRenamedNewHaven.description: The plantation general court of the Quinnipiac settlement renamed the town to New Haven Plantation.

wepowaugeSettled.name: Wepowauge settlement
wepowaugeSettled.description: The settlement at Wepowauge (later Milford) was formed by a land grant to English settlers from the Paugusset.

menunkatuckSettled.name: Menunkatuck settlement
menunkatuckSettled.description: The settlement at Menunkatuck (later Guilford) was formed by a land grant to English settlers from the Quinnipiac.

rippowamSettled.name: Rippowam settlement
rippowamSettled.description: Settlers from New Haven established Rippowam (later Stamford) on the North Fork of Long Island.

southdoldSettled.name: Southold settlement
southdoldSettled.description: Settlers from New Haven established Southdold on the North Fork of Long Island.

greenwichPurchase.name: Greenwich purchase
greenwichPurchase.description: New Haven purchased the land for Greenwich from the Siwanoy Indians.

newHavenColonyFormed.name: Formation of New Haven Colony
newHavenColonyFormed.description: New Haven Plantation, Stamford, Southhold, Milford, and Guilford were combined to form the New Haven Colony.

newHavenColonyJoinsNewEnglandConfederati.name: New Haven Colony joins the New England Confederation

branfordSettled.name: Branford settlement
branfordSettled.description: Settlers from Wethersfield, Connecticut Colony settled Branford and joined the New Haven Colony.

declarationOfIndependence.name: Declaration of Independence
declarationOfIndependence.description: On 04 July 1776, the Thirteen Colonies of the Kingdom of Great Britain in North America delcared their collective independence as the United States of America. The Declaration was ratified by the Second Continental Congress, with delegates from each of the thirteen colonies signing the declaration. The declaration was received by King George III, who declared that the colonies had committed an act of high treason against The Crown, and proclaimed the colonies to be in rebellion on 23 August 1775.
parties: Colony of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations

transfers.to: The Counties of New Castle, Kent and Sussex upon Delaware

areas: Colony of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations

transfers.to: State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations

creates: The Counties of New Castle, Kent and Sussex upon Delaware

delawareConstitution1776.name: Delaware Constitution of 1776
delawareConstitution1776.description: The Delaware Constitution of 1776 was the first document establishing the state government of Delaware. Following the declaration of independence of the Lower Colonies on the Delaware and reorganization as the Counties of New Castle, Kent and Sussex upon Delaware, ten members from each county met in a State Constitutional Convention on 27 August 1776. George Read and Thomas McKean contributed majorly to the constitution, which was enacted on 20 September 1776. After this, the convention dissolved. Among the changes made in the Constitution were the new name, "The Delaware State," the creation of the General Assembly of Delaware, the creation of the executive office of the President, and the creation of the state judiciary which would follow English Common Law.
parties: The Counties of New Castle, Kent and Sussex upon Delaware

areas: The Counties of New Castle, Kent and Sussex upon Delaware
transfers.from: The Counties of New Castle, Kent and Sussex upon Delaware

pennsylvaniaConstitution1776.name: Pennsylvania Constitution of 1776
pennsylvaniaConstitution1776.description: The Pennsylvania Constitution of 1776 was created to prevent the creation of an aristocratic class within the newly independent State of Pennsylvania based on the ideas of Thomas Paine's *Common Sense*. The constitutional convention met in Philadelphia and chose Benjamin Franklin as president and Colonel George Ross as vice president. The constitution was completed on 28 September 1776. The constitution has been called the most democratic document in North America, and contained several radical innovations. Voting was extended to all taxpayers (including African Americans), a unicameral, popularly-elected annual legislature was put in place, a Council of Census was elected to evaluate the state government, and several other resolutions inspired by the colonists' complaints against the British Crown were included.

declarationOfNewConnecticut.name: Declaration of Independence of New Connecticut
declarationOfNewConnecticut.description: New Connecticut was declared by delegates from 28 towns within the New Hampshire Grants of New York on 15 January 1777 or 17 January 1777. New Connecticut was not recognized by any foreign power, but was soon reorganized as the Vermont Republic and eventually admitted to the Union as the State of Vermont.

newConnecticutRenamedVermont.name: New Connecticut is renamed Vermont
newConnecticutRenamedVermont.description: The recently-declared and unrecognized New Connecticut is renamed as the Vermont Republic.

vermontClaimsEastUnion.name: The Vermont Republic claims the East Union of New Hampshire
vermontClaimsEastUnion.description: 16 towns on the western New Hampshire border petitioned to join the Vermont Republic, concerned that New Hampshire had focused too much on the coastal region. This claim was unrecognized by the New Hampshrie government.

vermontRescindsEastUnion.name: The Vermont Republic rescinds annexation of the East Union
vermontRescindsEastUnion.description: The Continental Congress pressured the Vermont Republic to rescind their claim to the East Union of New Hampshire, later declaring on 12 February 1779 that the East Union was always illegitimate.

massachusettsConstitution1780.name: Constitution of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts
massachusettsConstitution1780.description: In 1779, the Massachusetts Constitutional Convention began to draft a new constitution for the state. John Adams authored a draft on 30 October 1779 which was presented 15 June 1780 and ratified 25 October 1780 by the convention. It was the last state constitution to be written among the first thirteeen states, and was structured as a list of articles. This became a model for the United States Constitution seven years later. It declared the rights of citizens of the commonwealth, framed a government with a gubernatorial executive, bicameral legislature, and an independent judiciary, with a focus on the separation of powers between these entities.

articlesOfConfederation.name: Articles of Confederation

transfers.from: State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations

vermontClaimsEastUnion2.name: The Vermont Republic claims the East Union of New Hampshire

vermontClaimsWestUnion.name: The Vermont Republic claims the West Union of New York

vermontAbandonsEastUnionAndWestUnion.name: The Vermont Republic abandons its claim on the East Union and West Union

newYorkCedesErieTriangle.name: New York cedes its western claim to the federal government

westmorelandCountyDeclaredPennsylvania.name: Connecticut's claim to Westmoreland County assigned to Pennsylvania by the Congress of the Confederation
westmorelandCountyDeclaredPennsylvania.description: In an attempt to end the Pennamite–Yankee War, the Congress of the Confederation unanimously declared that the region of the Wyoming Valley claimed by Connecticut as Westmoreland County was part of Pennsylvania. As compensation, Connecticut was granted a claim to the Western Reserve of Ohio. Pennsylvania would refuse to confirm private land titles of settlers from Connecticut within the land, leading to the Second Pennamite–Yankee War, and the declaration of the State of Westmoreland in 1784. Connecticut would retain thier claim until 1786, when Pennsylvania confirmed the land titles and created Luzerne County.

virginiaCedesNorthwestClaim.name: Virginia cedes its claim northwest of the Ohio River to the federal government

pennsylvaniaVirginiaBorderAgreement.name: Pennsylvania and Virginia agree to a border between the states
pennsylvaniaVirginiaBorderAgreement.description: Pennsylvania and Virginia agree to a border continuing the Mason-Dixon Line to a point five degrees west of the Delaware River, then north. The agreement was approved by Virginia on 23 June 1783 and by Pennsylvania on 01 April 1784.

treatyOfParis1783.name: Treaty of Paris (1783)
treatyOfParis1783.description: In the Treaty of Paris, representatives of King George III and the United States officially negotiated the end of the rebellionary War. British North America would cease to claim the Thirteen Colonies, which would be recognized as the free, soverign, and independent United States of America. Boundaries between the remaining territory of British North America were defined, but some ambiguities would not be resolved until later treaties would establish final borders. Great Britain also ceded much of its western territory in the Ohio Valley to the United States, expanding the claims of the US into the Northwest Territory. This treaty, along with the Treaties of Versailles, marked the end of the First British Empire and the ascendency of the United States as a soverign nation.
parties: State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations

treatiesOfVersailles1783.name: Treaties of Versailles (1783)
treatiesOfVersailles1783.description: A component of the Peace of Paris, the Treaties of Versailles were signed among the colonial powers in North America. In this treaty, continental British colonies south of the United States were ceded to the Kingdom of Spain, and some minor territories in Africa and Europe were given to the Kingdom of France and the Kingdom of Spain.
parties: Republic of the Seven United Netherlands

declarationOfFranklin.name: Declaration of Independence of the State of Franklin

massachusettsCedesWesternClaim.name: Massachusetts cedes its western claim to the federal government

connecticutCedesWesternClaim.name: Connecticut cedes its western claim (except for the Western Reserve) to the federal government

massachusettsAbandonsWesternNewYorkClaim.name: Massachusetts abandons its claim to western New York

northwestTerritoryCreated.name: Creation of the Territory Northwest of the River Ohio

southCarolinaCedesWesternClaim.name: South Carolina cedes its western claim to the federal government

marylandCedesFederalDistrictTerritory.name: An act to cede to Congress a district of ten miles square in this state for the seat of government of the United States
marylandCedesFederalDistrictTerritory.description: Maryland cedes an area to the federal government for the purpose of establishing a seat of government in a federal territory. After the borders were set, Maryland formally ceded the specific parcel on 19 December 1791.

franklinPledgesAllegianceToNorthCarolina.name: The State of Franklin pledges allegance to North Carolina and dissolves

northwestTerritoryReorganized.name: The Northwest Territory is reorganized under the Constitution

virginiaCedesFederalTerritoryLand.name: Virginia cedes an area of ten square miles along the Potomac to the federal government to be used as the location of a national capital

northCarolinaCedesSouthwestTerritory.name: North Carolina cedes its claim west of the Great Smoky Mountains to the federal government

southwestTerritoryCreated.name: Creation of the Territory South of the River Ohio

residenceAct.name: Residence Act
residenceAct.description: Congress passed the Residence Act, approving the creation of a national capital on the Potomac River in a location selected by president George Washington.

vermontAdmittedToUnion.name: Vermont is admitted as the fourtheenth state of the Union

federalDistrictFormedFromMarylandAndVirg.name: A federal district is formed from a diamond ceded by Maryland and Virginia

marylandOfficiallyCedesFederalDistrict.name: Maryland officially cedes land along the Potomac to the federal government for the Federal District

pennsylvaniaPurchasesErieTriangle.name: Pennsylvania purchases the Erie Triangle from the federal government

kentuckyAdmittedToUnion.name: Kentucky is admitted as the fifteenth state of the Union

pinckneysTreaty.name: Pinckney's Treaty
pinckneysTreaty.description: Pinckney's Treaty, also called the Treaty of San Lorenzo or the Treaty of Madrid, was signed between the United States and the Kingdom of Spain to define the border between the US and Spanish Flordia, ending the first stage of the West Florida Controversy. Named for Thomas Pinckney, who negotiated with Spanish representative Don Manuel de Godoy, the treaty defined the boundaries of the United States around Spanish Florida and Spanish Louisiana, created rules for dealing with native peoples in Florida and Georgia, and ensured mutual defense of vessels on the Mississippi River and Gulf of Mexico.

tennesseeAdmittedToUnion.name: Tennessee is admitted as the sixteenth state, formed from the Southwest Territory

mississippiOrganicAct.name: Mississippi Territory organic act
mississippiOrganicAct.description: The federal government authorizes the creation of the Mississippi Territory in the land ceded from Spanish West Florida and the Georgia western claim. Georiga would continue to claim this land until the Compact of 1802, beginning the Yazoo land scandal.

stCroixRiverCommission.name: Commissioners agree on the source of the St. Croix River, setting the border of the District of Maine and British North America
stCroixRiverCommission.description: The far eastern border between British North America and the United States was defined by the St. Croix River, with a northward line from its source being the boundary between the Colony of New Brunswick and the District of Maine, held by the Commonwealth of Connecticut. In October 1798, commissioners from both nations agreed on the source of the river, establishing the final eastern boundary. The northern boundary would remain in periodic dispute until 1842.

areas: St. Croix River headwaters eastern claim

connecticutCedesWesternReserve.name: Connecticut cedes its claim to the Western Reserve
connecticutCedesWesternReserve.description: On 28 May 1800, the federal government passed an act accepting the cession of the Western Reserve from Connecticut. On 30 May 1800, Connecticut approved the cession and ceased its administration in all land west of Pennsylvania. After this, the ceded territory was *de facto* administered by the Northwest Territory.

inidanaTerritoryCreated.name: An act to divide the territory of the United States northwest of the Ohio, into two separate governments
inidanaTerritoryCreated.description: The Northwest Territory is divided on a line from the mouth of the Kentucky River to Fort Recovery and then north, with the western portion becoming the Indiana Territory

federalDistrictOrganized.name: An act concerning the District of Columbia
federalDistrictOrganized.description: Following the relocation of Congress to the federal district between Maryland and Virginia on 17 November 1800, the district was organized as the District of Columbia.

compactOf1802.name: Articles of Agreement and Cession (Compact of 1802)
compactOf1802.description: Following the authorization of negotiations between the federal government and the State of Georgia to resolve the Yazoo land scandal, the federal government paid 1.25 million dollars to Georgia in exchange for the cession of the state's western claim. The government also promised to extinguish American Indian land titles within Georiga. This was the final of the post-colonial land cessions by the original 13 states. At the same time, the federal government confirmed to Georiga the western region ceded by South Carolina which had been claimed by the state.

yazooLandsGrantedToMississippiTerritory.name: An act regulating the grants of land, and providing for the disposal of the lands of the United States, south of the state of Tennessee
yazooLandsGrantedToMississippiTerritory.description: Following the Compact of 1802, the federal government allowed for the lands ceded from Georiga to be granted to the Mississippi Territory. This would be completed on 27 March 1804.

ohioAdmittedToUnion.name: An act to enable the people of the eastern division of the territory northwest of the river Ohio to form a constitution and state government, and for the admission of such state into the Union, on equal footing with the original States, and for other purposes
ohioAdmittedToUnion.description: The southern half of the Northwest Territory and a sliver of the Indiana Territory are admitted as the seventeenth state, Ohio. The remainder of the Northwest Territory is annexed into the Indiana Territory. The western border is a line north from the mouth of the Great Miami River. The northern border is a line east from the southern tip of Lake Michigan, though the ohio constitution created a line from the southern tip of Lake Michigan to the northernmost cape of Maumee Bay, eventually leading to the Toledo War. President Thomas Jefferson signed the act approving Ohio's boundaries and constitution on 19 February 1803, but Congress did not pass a formal resolution to admit the state until 1953, at which time the date of statehood was set retroactively to 01 March 1803.

southwickJogCededByConnecticut.name: The Southwick Jog is ceded from Connecticut to Massachusetts
southwickJogCededByConnecticut.discription: Putting an end to long-standing border disagreements between Connecticut and Massachusetts, the Southwick Jog is ceded from Connecticut to Massachusetts. The final commissioners report was delivered on 30 November 1803, but no dates of government approval are known.

spanishLouisianaConveyal.name: Transfer of Spanish Southern Louisiana to French New Orleans
spanishLouisianaConveyal.description: Part of the Louisiana Purchase, Spanish officials officials formally conveyed the colonial lands of Southern Lousiana and their administration to France.

louisianaPurchase.name: Louisiana Purchase
louisianaPurchase.description: Directed by President Thomas Jefferson and negotated by James Monroe and Robert R. Livingston, the United States was on 11 April 1803 offered the aquisition of French Louisiana from the French First Republic for 80 million francs or 15 million dollars, including the cancellation of 20 million francs or 3.75 million dollars in French debt owed to US citizens. Occuring during the War of the Third Coalition, First Consul of France Napoleon Bonaparte adandoned plans to expand France's empire in the New World and did not wish to return the territory to Spain, instead deciding to sell the entire territory for cash to a neutral third party in the United States. The American negotiators, though only authorized to purchase the proximity of New Orleans for up to 10 million dollars, accepted the deal 19 days after it was offered. Britain, preferring the US hold the territory to France or another hostile continental power, allowed the deal to continue. President Jefferson and his cabinet debated the constitutionality of the deal for several months between July 1803 and October 1803, but decided against beginning the process of constitutional amendment to justify the purchase. Meanwhile in Congress, many Jeffersonians and most Federalists (mostly economic interests from New England) opposed the purchase, led by House Majority Leader John Randolph, but were unable to deny the purchase by a margin of two votes. Ultimately, the Senate consented to ratify the treaty with a vote of 24 to 7 on 20 October 1803, and authorized Jefferson to take possession of the territory and establish a temporary military government the following day. On 31 October 1803, Congress provided for local civil government as continuence of French and Spanish order in the territory, and plans were made for missions to explore and chart the territory. Throughout negotiation, the Kingdom of Spain had protested the purchase, arguing that France had promised not to alienate the territory to a third party and hadn't fulfilled their obligations under the Third Treaty of San Ildefonso to have all European powers recognize the King of Eturia. Madison responded by noting that the Spanish government had rescinded their right to negotiate over the territory to France before negotiations opened. Finally, on 30 November 1803, Spanish officials formally conveyed the colonial lands and their administration to France. Three weeks later on 20 December 1803, France turned over the historic colonial capital of New Orleans at the Cabildo, with the American flag being raised over Jackson Square. On 09 March 1804 and 10 March 1804, the Three Flags Day ceremony was conduced in St. Louis to transfer ownership of Upper Louisiana from Spain to France and then from France to the United States. The Louisiana Purchase extended the soverignty of the United States across the Missouri River, nearly doubling the nominal size of the country and leading to the creation of fifteen US states, corresponding today to 26% of the area of the contiguous United States.

threeFlagsCeremonySpainFrance.name: Three Flags Day ceremony of Spain and France
threeFlagsCeremonySpainFrance.description: Part of the Louisiana Purchase, Spain transfered ownership of Upper Louisiana to France. The following day, France would transfer the territory to the United States.

threeFlagsCeremonyFranceUS.name: Three Flags Day ceremony of France and the United States
threeFlagsCeremonyFranceUS.description: Part of the Louisiana Purchase, France transferred ownership of Upper Louisiana to the United States.

yazooLandsCededToMississippiTerritory.name: An act supplementary to the act intituled "An act regarding grants of land, and providing for the disposal of the lands of the United States, south of the state of Tennessee"
yazooLandsCededToMississippiTerritory.description: The Yazoo Lands between Tennessee and the Mississippi Territory previously ceded by Georiga were assigned to the Mississippi Territory.

orleansTerritoryOrganizedFromLouisianaPu.name: An act erecting Louisiana into two territories, and providing for the temporary government thereof
orleansTerritoryOrganizedFromLouisianaPu.description: Following the confirmation and transfer of the Louisiana Purchase, the Orleans Territory was organized from Lower Louisiana and the unorganized District of Louisiana was placed under the jurisdiction of the Indiana Territory

michiganTerritoryOrganized.name: An act to divide the Indiana Territory into two separate governments
michiganTerritoryOrganized.description: The Indiana Territory is divided along a line east from the southern tip of Lake Michigan and north from the lake's northern tip. The section north and east is organized as the Michigan Territory.

louisianaTerritoryOrganized.name: An act further providing for the government of the District of Louisiana
louisianaTerritoryOrganized.description: The District of Louisiana, previously under the jurisdiction of the Indiana Territory, is organized as the Louisiana Territory

illinoisTerritoryOrganized.name: An act for dividing the Indiana Territory into two separate governments
illinoisTerritoryOrganized.description: The Illinois Country, previously under the jurisdiction of the Indiana Territory, is organized as the Illinois Territory. A line between the Wabash River and Post Vincennes and then due north divided the Indiana Territory in the east (including a portion of the Upper Peninsula and Door Peninsula) from the new Illinois Territory in the west.

declarationOfWestFlorida.name: Declaration of Independence of West Florida
declarationOfWestFlorida.description: A portion of Spanish West Florida in the area claimed by the United States west of the Pearl River declares its independence as the State of Florida.

presidentalProclamation1810.name: Presidential Proclamation, 1810
presidentalProclamation1810.description: A part of the West Florida Controversy, Congress debated a course of action for the portion of West Florida claimed by the US as part of the Louisiana Purchase. During this time, several American filibuster excursions had attempted to claim the land for the United States, and a short-lived independent republic of mostly anglo-American tories had been proclaimed west of the Pearl River. On 27 October 1810, President James Madison proclaimed that the United States should move to take possession of West Florida between the Mississippi and Perdido rivers.

unitedStatesEnforcesWestFloridaClaim.name: Annexation of West Florida
unitedStatesEnforcesWestFloridaClaim.description: Following the Presidential Proclamation of 1810, William C. C. Claiborne and American forces were sent to take possession of West Florida between the Mississippi River and Perdido River. They entered the Republic of West Florida capital, St. Francisville, on 06 December 1810, and Baton Rouge on 10 December 1810, after which the Republic of West Florida, which had existed for less than two and a half months, promptly surrendered.

congressJointResolutionOnWestFloridaRepu.name: Joint resolution of Congress concerning the West Florida Republic
congressJointResolutionOnWestFloridaRepu.description: Following the American occupation of West Florida between the Mississippi River and Perdido River, claimed by Spanish West Florida and the independent Republic of West Florida, Congress passed a joint resolution on 15 January 1811 to provide for temporary occupation of the disputed territory subject to further negotiation. At this time, the Republic of West Florida was dissolved completely.

congressAuthorizationOfWestFloridaAnnexa.name: Congress authorizes annexation of the remainder of Spanish land west of the Perdido River
congressAuthorizationOfWestFloridaAnnexa.description: Congress authorized President James Madison in secret to take possession of all of Florida west of the Perdido River, including the use of military and naval forces as necessary. Historians today say this action is an early sign of the emergence of American imperialism and expeditionism.

batonRougeDistrictIncorporatedToOrleansT.name: The Baton Rouge district of West Florida is authorized by Congress to be incorporated to the Orleans Territory, soon to become the State of Louisiana

louisianaAdmittedToUnion.name: An act to enable the people of the Territory of Orleans to form a constitution and state government, and for the admission of such state into the Union, on equal footing with the original states, and for other purposes
louisianaAdmittedToUnion.description: The Orleans Territory, the southernmost section of the Louisiana Purchase, is allowed to form a state government and constitution, and is admitted as the eighteenth state, Louisiana. Some portions of the Orleans Territory, including the recently occupied Baton Rouge district and the northwestern frontier of the territory, are exceptions to this.

mobileDistrictAssignedToMississippiTerri.name: An act to enlarge the boundaries of the Mississippi Territory
mobileDistrictAssignedToMississippiTerri.description: With West Florida occupied, Congress assigned the Mobile district between the Pearl River and Perdido River to the Mississippi Territory.

batonRougeDistrictAddedToLouisiana.name: Baton Rouge district added to Louisiana
batonRougeDistrictAddedToLouisiana.description: The Baton Rouge district was added to the new State of Louisiana, as authorized by Congress on 14 April 1812. After this, all land of the former Orleans Territory was organized under other states or territories.

louisianaTerritoryReorganizedAsMissouriT.name: An act providing for the government of the Territory of Missouri
louisianaTerritoryReorganizedAsMissouriT.description: After the admittance of the State of Louisiana, the Louisiana Territory was reorganized as the Missouri Territory.

indianaAdmittedToUnion.name: An act to enable the people of the Indiana Territory to form a constitution and state government, and for the admission of such state into the Union on an equal footing with the original states
indianaAdmittedToUnion.description: Most of the Indiana Territory with parts of the Illinois Territory and Michigan Territory were admitted as the nineteenth state, Indiana. The Indiana northern tier was ceded from the Michigan Territory, and some land near the Wabash River was exchanged with the Illinois Territory. The portion of the Indiana Territory on the Upper Peninsula and Door Peninsula became unorganized.

alabamaTerritoryOrganizedFromMississippi.name: An act to establish a separate territorial government for the eastern part of the Mississippi Territory
alabamaTerritoryOrganizedFromMississippi.description: The Alabama Territory is organized by dividing the Mississippi Territory in half. Two approximately equal-sized parts similar in size to Georiga were created by dividing the territory along a straight line between Washington County to the Gulf of Mexico, after which the line continued generally north at an angle to keep the divisions roughly equal until it meets and follows the Tennessee River.

mississippiAdmittedToUnion.name: An act to enable the people of the western part of the Mississippi Territory to form a constitution and state government, and for the admission of such state into the union, on an equal footing with the original states
mississippiAdmittedToUnion.description: Following the division of the Mississippi Territory in half to create the Alabama Territory, the remainder of the Mississippi Territory is admitted as the twentieth state, Mississippi. At this time, the southern panhandle of the state was still technically occupied from Spanish West Florida.

fortStMarksIncursion.name: Capture of Fort St. Marks by Andrew Jackson's army
fortStMarksIncursion.description: As part of the First Seminole War, which began sometime in 1814, Colonel Andrew Jackson gathered about four thousand regulars, volunteers, militia, and friendly native allies to begin an excursion into Spanish East Florida. Setting out from Fort Scott and entering Florida on 15 March 1818, they followed the Apalachiola River and constructed Fort Gadsden before burning the Red Stick village at Tallahasee and taking two Native American prisoners. By 06 April 1818, Jackson's army had reached Fort St. Marks, which they seized from the Spanish the following day.

fortBarrancasAndPensacolaIncursion.name: Capture of Fort Barrancas and Pensacola by Andrew Jackson's army
fortBarrancasAndPensacolaIncursion.description: Following the capture of Fort St. Marks, General Andrew Jackson left Fort Gadsden with one thousand men on 07 May 1818 towards Pensacola, the capital of Spanish West Florida. Upon reaching the city on 23 May 1818, the Spanish governor and 175-man garrison retreated to Fort Barrancas. After a few-day-long siege, the Spanish surrendered Fort Barrancas on 28 May 1818.

treatyOfGhent.name: Treaty of Ghent
treatyOfGhent.description: Ending the War of 1812 between the United States and the United Kingdom, the Treaty of Ghent included the exchanging for a few islands in the Maritimes.
parties: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

transfers.from: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

transfers.to: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

illinoisAdmittedToUnion.name: An act to enable the people of the Illinois Territory to form a constitution and state government, and for the admission of such state into the Union on an equal footing with the original states
illinoisAdmittedToUnion.description: The half of the Illinois Territory south of 42°30′ was admitted as the twenty-first state, Illinois. The remaining part of the Illinois Territory and the portions of Door Peninsula and the Upper Peninsula which had been a part of the Indiana Territory were assigned to the Michigan Territory

treatyOf1818.name: Treaty of 1818
treatyOf1818.description: The Treaty of 1818 (also called the "Convention respecting fisheries, boundary and the restoration of slaves," the London Convention, the Anglo-American Convention of 1818, or the Convention of 1818) was signed between the United States and the United Kingdom to resolve boundary issues, allow for joint occupation and settlement in the Oregon Country, and regulated fishing and commerce between the counties, among other purposes.
parties: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

transfers.from: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

transfers.to: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

arkansawTerritoryOrganizedFromMissouriTe.name: An act establishing a separate territorial government in the southern part of the Territory of Missouri
arkansawTerritoryOrganizedFromMissouriTe.description: The Missouri Territory is divided by a line starting where the Mississippi River meets 36° north, and from there west to the St. Francis River, following it to 36°30′ north, then west. The area south of this line is organized as the Arkansaw Territory

alabamaAdmittedToUnion.name: An act to enable the people of the Alabama Territory to form a constitution and state government, and for the admission of such state into the Union on an equal footing with the original states
alabamaAdmittedToUnion.description: The Alabama Territory was admitted as the twenty-second state, Alabama. The southern panhandle of the state, like in Mississippi, was still technically occupied from Spanish West Florida at this time, but negotiations of the Adams–Onís Treaty had been underway since the beginning of 1819.

maineAdmittedToUnion.name: An act for the admission of the State of Maine into the Union
maineAdmittedToUnion.description: The District of Maine, which was a part of Massachusetts, was admitted as the twenty-third state, Maine. This was part of the Missouri Compromise, in which Missouri would be admitted as a slave state and Maine as a free state to keep the balance of power between Northern and Southern influences.

arkansasTerritoryRenamed.name: An act relative to the Arkansas Territory

adamsOnisTreaty.name: Adams–Onís Treaty
adamsOnisTreaty.description: The Adams–Onís Treaty resolved the West Florida Controversy and the Florida invasion during the First Seminole War. The United States aquired the remaining land of Spanish West Florida, which had been invaded based on a claim stemming from the Louisiana Purchase, and Spanish East Florida, which had been the site of some incursions in the First Seminole War. Signed 22 February 1819 by John Quincy Adams, the United States agreed to renounce claims to Spanish Texas in exchange for the transfer of East and West Florida, while the Spanish withdrew claims to the Oregon Country. The treaty came into effect on 22 February 1821.

eastFloridaTransferred.name: Spanish East Florida is formally transferred to the United States
eastFloridaTransferred.description: As negotiated in the Adams–Onís Treaty, Spanish East Florida was transferred to the United States by Spain on 10 July 1821.

westFloridaTransferred.name: Spanish West Florida is formally transferred to the United States
westFloridaTransferred.description: As negotiated in the Adams–Onís Treaty, Spanish West Florida was transferred to the United States by Spain on 17 July 1821.

missouriAdmittedToUnion.name: An act to authorize the people of the Missouri Territory to form a constitution and state government, and for the admission of such state into the Union on an equal footing with the original states, and to prohibit slavery in certain territories
missouriAdmittedToUnion.description: The southeastern corner of the Missouri Territory was admitted as the twenty-fourth state, Missouri. This was part of the Missouri Compromise, in which Missouri would be admitted as a slave state and Maine as a free state to keep the balance of power between Northern and Southern influences. The remaining part of the Missouri Territory became unorganized.

floridaTerritoryOrganized.name: An act for the establishment of a territorial government in Florida
floridaTerritoryOrganized.description: With the completion of the transfer of East Florida and West Florida from Spain to the United States, Congress authorized the organization of the Florida Territory.

moveArkansasTerritoryWesternBorder1.name: An act to fix the western boundary line of the Territory of Arkansas, and for other purposes
moveArkansasTerritoryWesternBorder1.description: The western border of the Arkansas Territory was moved eastwards to a line south from a point 40 miles west of the new state of Missouri's western border. Territory which was previously in the Arkansas Territory becomes unorganized.

russianAmericaSouthernBoundaryAgreement.name: Russian America southern boundary agreements
russianAmericaSouthernBoundaryAgreement.description: The boundary between Russian America and the Oregon Country was set at 54°40′ north in two separate treaties between Russia and the United States and Russia and the United Kingdom.
parties: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

moveArkansasTerritoryWesternBorder2.name: Cede western land of the Arkansas Territory to the Cherokee

treatyOfGhentArbitration.name: First Treaty of Ghent Arbitration
treatyOfGhentArbitration.description: As per the terms of the Treaty of Ghent, the United States and United Kingdom appealed to King William I of the Netherlands to arbitrate the disputed border between Maine and British North America. The King, finding reconciling the treaty with the maps too difficult, drew a new compromise line favorable to the United Kingdom instead. The United Kingdom accepted it, but the United States rejected it.
parties: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

declarationOfIndianStreamRepublic.name: Declaration of Independence of the Republic of Indian Stream
declarationOfIndianStreamRepublic.description: A region of New Hampshire north of the Connecticut Lakes, disputed between the United Kingdom and the United States, declared independence as the Republic of Indian Stream.

michiganTerritoryExpansion.name: An act to attach the territory of the United States west of the Mississippi river, and north of the state of Missouri, to the Territory of Michigan
michiganTerritoryExpansion.description: A large region of unorganized territory north of Missouri stretching from the Mississippi River to the Missouri River and White Earth River was assigned to the Michigan Territory.

indianStreamRepublicRecognizesNewHampshi.name: Republic of Indian Stream recognizes jurisdiction of New Hampshire
indianStreamRepublicRecognizesNewHampshi.description: Threatened with invasion by the sheriff of Coös County, New Hampshire, the assembly of the Republic of Indian Stream capitulated to New Hampshire and ceased to operate independently the following day. The dispute over the land between the United States and United Kingdom was not resolved until the Webster–Ashburton Treaty.

arkansasAdmittedToUnion.name: An act for the admission of the State of Arkansas into the Union, and to provide for the due execution of the laws of the United States, within the same, and for other purposes
arkansasAdmittedToUnion.description: The Arkansas Territory was admitted as the twenty-fifth state, Arkansas.

ohioNorthernSurvey.name: An act to settle and establish the northern boundary line of the State of Ohio
ohioNorthernSurvey.description: The survey of the northern border of the State of Ohio, including the Toledo Strip, was approved. The disputed region between Ohio and Michigan had gradually come under more tension since 1820, with various attempts at federal land surveys in the area leading to inconclusive results. In 1833, Congress rejected Michigan's request for a state constitutional convention because of the dispute, leading to calls for an unauthorized convention in the territory by Michigan Governor Stevens T. Mason. In February 1835, Ohio set up county governments in the Toledo Strip and named the county after incumbent Governor Robert Lucas. Six days later, Michigan responded with the Pains and Penalties Act, making it a criminal offense with harsh penalties for Ohioans to carry out the duties of government within the Strip. Brigadier General Joseph W. Brown of the Third U.S. Brigade brought the Michigan state militia into the Strip, beginning the Toledo War. On 31 March 1835, Governor Lucas and General John Bell led six hundred fully armed Ohio militiamen to Perrysburg, Ohio, ten miles southwest of Toledo. At the same time, Governor Mason and General Brown arrived to occupy the city of Toledo with around one thousand armed men to prevent the border from being marked. At this point, President Andrew Jackson and Attorney General Benjamin Butler calculated that keeping the Toledo Strip as part of Ohio would be politically advantageous for his party and declined to take the issue to the Supreme Court, instead sending two representatives to arbitrate the conflict. On April 7, a re-survey was recommended to mark the Harris Line, claimed by Ohio. The Ohio militia, thinking peace had been achieved, disbanded and began to hold elections in the region as required by Ohio law. Mason, however, refused the deal and continued preparing for armed conflict. The elections were contentious, with Ohio officials harrassed by Michigan authorities and residents threatened with arrest if they participated. A Michigan sherriff indeed arrested two Ohio partisans under the Pains and Penalties Act. Lucas sent surveyors to mark the Harris line, who were attacked by 50 to 60 members of General Brown's militia in the Battle of Phillips Corners. Nine Ohioans were taken prisoner in a sabbath-day retreat. The Ohio legislature passed an act further establishing Ohio's authority in the Strip, including making Toledo the capital of Lucas County with a Court of Common Pleas and a budget of $300,000 to implement Ohio state law; Michigan responded with a budget of $315,000 for its militia in the area. Despite the lack of an enabling act of Congress, Michigan drafted a state constitution with provisions for a functional state government. In Ohio, ten thousand volunteers called the "Ohio million" joined the militia and travelled north. For the next several months, partisans on both sides engaged in skirmishes, retaliatory battles in the courts, and espionage on opposing county sherriffs. On 15 July 1835, Deputy Sherrif Joseph Wood of Monroe County, Michigan, was stabbed non-lethally by the son of Major Benjamin Stickney durring an arrest.

wisconsinTerritoryOrganized.name: An act establishing the territorial government of Wisconsin
wisconsinTerritoryOrganized.description: The Wisconsin Territory was organized from the western portion of the Michigan Territory. The Michigan peninsula and most of the Upper Peninsula remained in the Michigan Territory in anticipation of the admittance of Michigan as a state.

michiganAbandonsToledoStrip.name: Frostbitten Convention
michiganAbandonsToledoStrip.description: In August 1835, Jackson removed Mason as Michigan's territorial governor and appinted John S. Horner. As the replacement governor was inbound, Stevens T. Mason ordered one thousand militiament to enter Toledo and prevent the Court of Common Pleas from joining. The judges held a midnight court before retreating south to Ohio forces. Governor Horner was extremely unpopular in Michigan and was soon voted out of the office, with Mason being again elected as governor. Jackson signed a bill allowing Michigan's admission into the Union as a free state on the condition that they cede the Toledo Strip to Ohio. In exchange, Michigan would be granted most of the Upper Peninsula, an offer which was rejected by a special commission in Ann Arbor. Due to the high expenses of the militia, Michigan soon faced near bankruptcy and realized they would be ineligable for benefits from the 1836 surplus. This led to the acceptance of Congress's terms by a second convention in Ann Arbor on 14 December 1836, which was itself not without contention. Congress questioned the convention's legality but accepted the results of this "Frostbitten Convention," marking the end of the Toledo War.

michiganAdmittedToUnion.name: An act to establish the northern boundary line of the State of Ohio, and to provide for the admission of the State of Michigan into the Union upon the conditions therein expressed
michiganAdmittedToUnion.description: The Michigan Territory was admitted as the twenty-sixth state, Michigan. Michigan had applied to have a state constitutional convention in 1933 but had been rejected because of their ongoing conflict with the State of Ohio over the Toledo Strip. In December 1836, the Frostbitten Convention accepted Congress's terms and abandoned the Toledo Strip in exchange for land in the Upper Peninsula.

plattePurchase.name: Platte Purchase
plattePurchase.description: The Platte Purchase was obtained from several nations including the Potawatomi, Iowa, Missouria, Otoe, Sauk, and Meskwaki. This land was ceded to Missouri, extending its northern border west to the Missouri River.

iowaTerritoryOrganized.name: An act to divide the Territory of Wisconsin and to establish the territorial government of Iowa
iowaTerritoryOrganized.description: The Iowa Territory was organized from the Wisconsin Territory west of the Mississippi River

missouriClaimsIowaBorderTerritory.name: Missouri claims an area north of its border with the Iowa Territory
missouriClaimsIowaBorderTerritory.description: Based on a combination of survey misunderstandings, a misreading of Native American treaties, and unclear wording in the Missouri Constitution, The State of Missouri claimed a northern border line nine and a half miles north of the southern border line claimed by the Iowa Territory.

websterAshburtonTreaty.name: Webster–Ashburton Treaty
websterAshburtonTreaty.description: After several decades of border issues between the United States and British North America, the Webster–Ashburton Treaty was negotiated in Washington, D.C. by Daniel Webster and Lord Ashburton and signed by President John Tyler. The treaty resolved border conflicts which had caused skirmishes between Americans and New Brunswickers in the Aroostook War in 1838 and 1839. This included the settlement of the Maine–New Brunswick international border, the international border between Lake Superior and the Lake of the Woods, confirmation of the southern boundary of the Province of Quebec, reaffirmation of the 49th parallel westerward through the Rocky Mountains, shared use of the Great Lakes, and a committment to ending the intercontinental slave trade.
parties: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

transfers.to: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

transfers.from: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

floridaAdmittedToUnion.name: An act for the admission of the States of Iowa and Florida into the Union
floridaAdmittedToUnion.description: The Florida Territory was admitted as the twenty-seventh state, Florida.

texasRepublicAnnexed.name: Joint Resolution for annexing Texas to the United States
texasRepublicAnnexed.description: Part of the platform of President James K. Polk was the annexation of Texas, which had declared itself an independent republic from Mexico in 1836. Texas claimed land north of the Rio Grande, but only controlled land north of the Nueces River. The United States inherited this border dispute upon the annexation of the Republic of Texas. This would lead to the Mexican–American War the next year.

texasAdmittedToUnion.name: Joint Resolution for the admission of the State of Texas into the Union
texasAdmittedToUnion.description: Following the annexation of Texas a few months prior, Texas formally handed over soverignty in a ceremony in February 1846, becoming the twenty-eighth state. Mexico's claim to Texas would remain, leading to the Mexican–American War a few months later.

thorntonAffair.name: Thornton Affair
thorntonAffair.description: The Thornton Affair involved 2000 Mexican cavalry attack and rout a 70-man US patrol in contested territory between the Rio Grande and Nueces River. This was a primary justification for President James K. Polk's call to Congress to declare the Mexican–American War.

battleOfPaloAlto.name: Battle of Palo Alto
battleOfPaloAlto.description: A few days after the Thornton Affair, Mexican artillery at Matamoros opened fire on Fort Texas for 160 hours while gathering forces. On 08 May 1846, General Zachary Taylor and 2,400 troops arrived to relieve the fort and were intercepted by General Arista and 3,400 Mexican troops north of the Rio Grande. In response to the American "flying artillery", the Mexicans retreated during the night.

battleOfResacaDeLaPalma.name: Battle of Resaca de la Palma
battleOfResacaDeLaPalma.description: After the Mexican retreat in the Battle of Palo Alto, they took position on the far side of a dry riverbed. Hand-to-hand combat occured the following day, and the US Cavalry captured the Mexican artillery. The  Mexicans began to retreat and were routed as they were forced to abandon their artillery and baggage. Further casualties were inflicted at Fort Brown and at the Rio Grande during the retreat, resulting in a major American victory and the end of the Texas campaign.

declarationOfMexicanAmericanWar.name: Declaration of the Mexican–American War
declarationOfMexicanAmericanWar.description: After hearing of the Thornton Affiar, President Polk said in a message to Congress: "The cup of forbearance had been exhausted even before the recent information from the frontier of the Del Norte. But now, after reiterated menaces, Mexico has passed the boundary of the United States, has invaded our territory and shed American blood upon the American soil. She has proclaimed that hostilities have commenced, and that the two nations are now at war." Despite protests by Whig members of Congress, the declaration of war was approved on 13 May 1846.

newMexicoCampaign.name: New Mexico Campaign
newMexicoCampaign.description: After the declaration of the Mexican–American War on 13 May 1846, Army General Stephen W. Kearny led the 1700-strong Army of the West from Fort Leavenworth, Kansas in June 1846 into New Mexico. Encountering no resistance, they entered Santa Fe on 15 August 1846 and claimed the New Mexico Territory for the United States. On 18 August 1846, Kearny declared himself the military governor and established a civilian government for the territory.

taosRevolt.name: Taos Revolt
taosRevolt.description: After the departure of General Kearny from Santa Fe, dissenters began plotting an uprising against the occupying American forces. The revolt began in Don Fernando de Taos, led by Pablo Montoya and Tomás Romero. The military governor of the territory, Charles Bent, was killed on the same day.

areas: Santa Gertrudis de lo de Mora

battleOfCanada.name: Battle of Cañada
battleOfCanada.description: Colonal Price led 353 soldiers north from Santa Fe to counter the Taos Revolt. They met along the road to Santa Cruz de la Cañada, where three strong houses at the base of a hill were held by the revolters. With artillery and an uphill cavalry charge, the Americans were able to dislodge the rebel positions. Some leaders of the revolt were killed or captured, and the rebels returned to Taos.

battleOfEmbudoPass.name: Battle of Embudo Pass
battleOfEmbudoPass.description: Following the Battle of Cañada, Colonel Price advanced up the Rio del Norte to Luceros, where his forces were reinforced. On 29 January 1847, Price marched to La Joya, where a force of eighty insurgents were emposted. Captain John H. K. Burgwin discovered the insurgents at El Embudo in strong defensive positions. Several flanking maneuvers forced the revolters into retreat to El Embudo, where they surrendered.

siegeOfPuebloDeTaos.name: Siege of Pueblo de Taos
siegeOfPuebloDeTaos.description: After the defeat of revolters at the Battle of Cañada and Battle of Embudo Pass, Corporal Price and his forces moved to Pueblo de Taos, the center of insurgent activity. American forces throughout the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, including Taos Mountain, encountered and dispatched revolters. The rebels had strongly fortified Pueblo de Taos, which Price countered with a two-and-a-half hour artillery battery. Dragoons and mounted soldiers were placed around the insurgent encampment to prevent escape to the mountains. After another two hours of battery, a storming was ordered on the church. After some difficulty, the church was captured and artillery began to fire grapeshot through the fortifications, at which time the rebels abandoned the western part of the town. The following day, the rebels surrendered their leader, Tomás Romero. After this, two small skirmishes occured at the Battle of Red River Canyon, the Las Vegas Affiar, and the Battle of Cienega Creek, but organized resistance to American occupation was eliminated.

bearFlagRevolt.name: Bear Flag Revolt
bearFlagRevolt.description: 33 rebels, mostly American pioneers, within Mexican-owned Alta California staged a revolt and siezed the garrison at Sonoma Barracks north of San Francisco Bay. They proclaimed the California Republic and raised the "Bear Flag" over Sonoma. Soon after, United States Army Captain John C. Frémont would arrive to support the rebels.

battleOfMonterey.name: Battle of Monterey
battleOfMonterey.description: Upon the beginning of the Mexican–American War, the USS Savannah*, USS *Cyane*, and USS *Levant* were already in the Monterey harbor. Commodore John Drake Sloat ordered the Pacific Squadron to capture ports in northern Alta California, including the capital city of Monterey. The three ships captured the city without firing a shot.

unitedStatesControlsSonoma.name: United States flag is raised over Sonoma Barracks
unitedStatesControlsSonoma.description: Following the proclamation of the California Republic in Sonoma, Alta California, the United States arrived to support the rebellion. On 05 July 1846, the Republic's military of one to two hundred men were subsumed into the US California Batallion. On 09 July 1846, US Navy Lieutenant Joseph Revere raised the United States flag over the Sonoma Barracks and Sutter's Fort, marking the end of the Bear Flag Revolt and the Republic of California

battleOfYerbaBuena.name: Battle of Yerba Buena
battleOfYerbaBuena.description: On 09 July 1846, the USS *Portsmouth* berthed at Sausalito captured Yerba Buena, near modern San Francisco, without firing a shot.

oregonTreaty.name: Oregon Treaty
oregonTreaty.description: The Oregon Treaty established the 49th parallel between the Lake of the Woods and the Pacific as the continental border of British and American holdings, ending the sharing of the Oregon Country. The treaty specified that a strait between Vancouver Island and the continent should be the maritime border, but did not name any one strait, leading to a dispute over the San Juan Islands.
parties: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

captureOfSanDiego.name: Capture of San Diego
captureOfSanDiego.description: John C. Frémont under the orders of Commodore Stockton moved his batallion to San Diego, landing on 29 July 1846 and raising the US flag over the city.

captureOfLosAngeles.name: Capture of Los Angeles
captureOfLosAngeles.description: Commodore Robert F. Stockton, commander of the Pacific Squadron, entered Los Angeles unopposed and took control of the city.

californiaAnnexationProclamation.name: Proclamation of the annexation of California into the United States
californiaAnnexationProclamation.description: Following the capture of Monterey, Yerba Buena (soon to be renamed San Francisco), San Diego, and Los Angeles, Commodore Stockton issued a proclamation that California was a part of the United States on 17 August 1846

iowaAdmittedToUnion.name: An act for the admission of the State of Iowa into the Union
iowaAdmittedToUnion.description: The portion of the Iowa Territory south of 43°30′ north and east of the Big Sioux River was admitted as the twenty-ninth state, Iowa. The border conflict with Missouri was not resolved at this time.

alexandriaCountyRetrocededToVirginia.name: District of Columbia retrocession
alexandriaCountyRetrocededToVirginia.description: The State of Virginia had ceded Alexandria County to the federal government to be used for the federal district. Residents of Arlington had long debated about the disenfranchisement that came with citizenship of the district, and percieved Congress to be negligent to the District of Columbia, and petitioned for the land to be retroceded to Virginia in 1847. The remaining part of the District was east of the Potomac, about 68 square miles in area.

wisconsinAdmittedToUnion.name: An act to enable the people of Wisconsin Territory to form a constitution and state government, and for the admission of such state into the Union
wisconsinAdmittedToUnion.description: The southern part of the Wisconsin Territory was admitted as the thirtieth state, Wisconsin. The remaining section of the Wisconsin territory retained a civil government with a delegate to the House of Representatives.

treatyOfGuadalupeHidalgo.name: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
treatyOfGuadalupeHidalgo.description: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ended the Mexican–American War. Signed on 02 February 1848 in the town of Guadalupe Hidalgo near Mexico City. After the Mexican army was defeated and the capital captured in September 1847, Mexico entered negotiations with the US envoy, Nicholas Trist. Mexico ceded 55% of its territory, with the US acquiring land that would make up seven states. Mexico also relinquished claims to Texas and recognized the Rio Grande as its southern boundary. The US government paid Mexico 15 million dollars and paid debts owed to American citizens by the Mexican government, and allowed for either relocation or full civil rights of citizens in the annexed territory. Ratifications were exchanged on 30 May 1848, and the treaty was proclaimed on 04 July 1848. In the Senate, the Whig party opposed the war and rejected manifest destiny. Despite this opposition, the Senate ratified the treaty with a vote of 38 to 16. The land gained would be increased with the Gadsden Purchase of 1853.

oregonTerritoryOrganized.name: An act to establish the territorial government of Oregon

honeyWarResolved.name: The Supreme Court resolves the border of Missouri and Iowa
honeyWarResolved.description: The Supreme Court resolved the Honey War between Iowa and Missouri, using the Sullivan Line as the interstate border. This line is a jog roughly splitting the disputed area, and was the line which existed before the dispute. This status quo was accepted by both states.

minnestoaTerritoryOrganized.name: An act to establish the territorial government of Minnesota
minnestoaTerritoryOrganized.description: All of the land operating *de facto* as the Wisconsin Territory, as well as unorganized territory east of the Missouri River and White Earth River, are organized as the Minnesota Territory

deseretFormation.name: Formation of the State of Deseret
deseretFormation.description: Settlers in the southwest claim a portion of the land taken in the Mexican-American War as the State of Deseret, led by leaders of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (Mormon Church). These settlers' petition to be admitted to the United States as a state was rejected by Congress.

californiaAdmitted.name: An act for the admission of the State of California into the Union
californiaAdmitted.description: The western portion of the Mexican Cession was admitted as the thirty-first state, California.

utahTerritoryOrganized.name: An act to establish a territorial government for Utah

ukCedesHorseshoeReefRock.name: Treaty on the Canadian Boundary, with the United Kingdom
ukCedesHorseshoeReefRock.description: The United Kingdom ceded a very small area of underwater rock for a lighthouse near Buffalo. The lighthouse was named for nearby Horseshoe Reef.
parties: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

transfers.from: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

texasWesternClaimNewMexicoTerritoryOrgan.name: An act proposing to the State of Texas the establishment of her northern and western boundaries, the relinquishment by the said state of all territory claimed by her exterior to said boundaires, and of all her claims upon the United States, and to establish a territorial government for New Mexico
texasWesternClaimNewMexicoTerritoryOrgan.description: The federal government purchased Texas' western claim and organized the New Mexico Territory from part of the land.

dissolutionOfDeseret.name: Dissolution of the State of Deseret
dissolutionOfDeseret.description: After the creation of the Utah Territory, the State of Deseret dissolved itself. On 03 February 1851, Brigham Young, 2nd President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints, would be inaugurated as the first territorial Governor of Utah.

washingtonTerritoryOrganized.name: An act to establish the territorial government of Washington
washingtonTerritoryOrganized.description: The half of the Oregon Territory north of 46° and the Columbia River was organized as the Washington Territory.

creationOfGreerCounty.name: Creation of Greer County, Texas
creationOfGreerCounty.description: An innacuraccy in the Adams–Onís Treaty of 1819 led to a conflicting interpretation of which river fork should be considered the "Red River" to determine the northern border of Texas. The State of Texas claimed Greer County based on the North Fork, while the United States claimed the land based on the South Fork. This would be resolved by the Supreme Court in 1896.
